falsifier: Exhibit a case where a target-side lbl_<ADDR> blob and our named global share a base address, the six-field tiling arithmetic holds, and the linked bytes nevertheless differ -- that would show base equality is insufficient and the guards are right to refuse. Conversely the law is DISPROVED as stated if regnorm is shown to already resolve blob-vs-split base equality (run it on any other function whose TU splits a dtk bss blob and check whether the STRUCTURAL row is reported as genuine). subject: project:gdl
value:
A TARGET-SIDE ANONYMOUS dtk BLOB AND OUR FINER NAMED SPLIT ARE BASE-EQUAL, AND BOTH RELOCATION GUARDS OVER-FIRE ON THE PAIR. This is the mirror of the already-recorded own-pool ghost case, and it is a measurement of the GUARDS as much as of the function (AGENTS.md discipline 14).

THE SHAPE. dtk names a .bss region it cannot subdivide with one placeholder, `lbl_<ADDR>`, sized to the whole run. A TU that reconstructs that region as several real C globals emits its relocation against the FIRST of them. The two reloc rows then read `lbl_<ADDR>` on the target side against a concrete C identifier on ours, which is neither the anonymous-vs-anonymous shape that fndiff's MATCH-MODULO-RELOC-NAMING verdict absorbs, nor a wrong-symbol bug.

MEASURED INSTANCE, game/boss/boss.c::BossDeath. fndiff --clean labelled it OPERAND_DIFF with '4 real diff lines' while its own line already said 'raw rows 8, of which 0 non-reloc -- 0 is the real'; regnorm printed `2 STRUCTURAL (2 genuine)` with the annotation `[reloc target differs]`, the exact signature of the btricol wrong-symbol bug that regnorm-is-the-only-screen-that-sees-a-wrong-reloc-symbol was written for. Both refusals were CORRECT BY THEIR OWN LOGIC and both were wrong about the function. symbols.txt carries HealthMeterBG at .bss:0x8023E608 size 0x18 and then a single blob lbl_8023E620 size 0x54; boss.c declares six consecutive globals from 0x8023E620 -- 0x18 + 0xC + 0xC + 0xC + 0xC + 0xC = 0x54 exactly, every declared address equal to the running sum, and the next declaration gSpewItems landing at 0x8023E674 = base + 0x54. HealthMeterFG's base IS lbl_8023E620's base.

THE DECISION PROCEDURE, and it costs no build. When a reloc row reads `lbl_<ADDR>` against one of your own named globals: (1) look up the blob's SIZE in symbols.txt; (2) sum the sizes of your consecutive declarations starting at that address; (3) check that the sums tile the blob exactly and that the next declaration lands at base+size. Tiles exactly => base-equal, the row is a naming artifact and the function's `real` of 0 is the truth. Does not tile => you have a genuine wrong-symbol or wrong-size defect and the guards were right; go read the btricol law.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT PROVE, stated because a green DOL proves little here: boss.c is a NonMatching Object, so its BSS is never linked, and the base equality rests on the TU's own declaration order under -common on (which links reverse-order -- see the BSS reverse-declaration-order hazard). Base equality is an argument about addresses in symbols.txt, not a link gate. The gate arrives only when the TU flips.

CONSEQUENCE. Do not record a `[reloc target differs]` row as a defect, and do not record it as noise, until the tiling arithmetic has been run and PRINTED. Two runs have now spent effort on rows of this class -- run 32 read one as a report-vs-fndiff disagreement, this run read one as a candidate wrong-symbol bug -- and in both cases the deciding fact was three lines of arithmetic over symbols.txt that no score computes.
